data.title: GIC in talks to lease bulk of 88,000 sq ft CapitaSky space to be vacated by Allianz
data.description:
[SINGAPORE] Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund GIC is said to be in talks to lease some three floors of space in the CapitaSky building at 79 Robinson Road to be vacated by Allianz.

Allianz’ existing lease at CapitaSky for about 88,000 square feet (sq ft) – on three whole floors and a part floor – ends in March 2027. GIC is said to be looking at the three full floors adding up to 75,000 sq ft.

The 29-storey building is 70 per cent owned by CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust (CICT), with CapitaLand Open End Real Estate Fund holding the remaining 30 per cent. The building received its Temporary Occupation Permit in April 2020.

In May, The Business Times reported that Allianz – one of the world’s leading insurers and asset managers – will move to Shaw Tower in Beach Road from CapitaSky. The space to be vacated by Allianz was said to be garnering strong leasing interest.

In August, at CICT’s first-half results briefing, CICT’s manager said it is in discussions with prospective tenants for the Allianz space in CapitaSky, including existing ones seeking to expand within the building.

BT understands that the Allianz space is no longer being marketed, triggering talk that GIC, which is at Capital Tower across the road, may be the next occupier of the space.

The sovereign fund is said to be on the expansion path.

GIC is a major tenant at the CICT-owned Capital Tower; and is said to occupy about 280,500 sq ft at the 52-storey building, which was completed in 2000 and has undergone refurbishments over the years. “GIC declines to comment,” said a spokesperson.

A seasoned office market watcher commented that it would not be surprising if GIC is in talks to take over the Allianz space in CapitaSky: “GIC has growth plans and it is unable to expand further in Capital Tower, which already has very high occupancy. It makes sense to expand to CapitaSky, which is just across the street.”

GIC currently also leases two floors totalling about 24,000 sq ft at the Afro-Asia building at 63 Robinson Road. The office market watcher said the lease might have been a stop-gap solution to accommodate GIC’s immediate need for more space.

“GIC may eventually consolidate its operations from the Afro-Asia building into the CapitaSky space, if it inks a lease there,” he added.

Leasing deals at Newport Tower, The Clifford

Separately, at Newport Tower being built in Anson Road, global engineering and architecture firm Arup is said to be in advanced talks to lease two office floors totalling about 63,000 sq ft of net lettable area.

Newport Tower is the 220,000 sq ft office component of City Developments Ltd’s (CDL) mixed-used project Newport Plaza.

The offices will be on eight floors – levels two to nine – of the 45-storey project, which will include upmarket residences for sale, branded serviced apartments and retail space.

Newport Tower is expected to be completed in Q4 2027.

Arup’s relocation to Newport Tower will be an expansion; it currently occupies about 40,000 sq ft at Frasers Tower in Cecil Street.

As its lease for this space is also said to expire in Q4 2027, Arup will need a short extension on its lease at Frasers Tower to facilitate its move to Newport Tower.

Word on the street is that Arup is being offered a more attractive rental at Newport Tower than the estimated S$12-13 per square foot a month for a lease renewal in Frasers Tower.

Additionally, the package it is being offered by CDL is likely to include a rental cap upon lease renewal.

At Singapore Land Group’s The Clifford in Raffles Place, which is currently under development, commercial insurance broker Aon is said to have leased two floors totalling about 40,000 sq ft in the low zone of the 34-storey building, with an option to take more space.

Scheduled for completion in the second half of 2028, The Clifford will have 21 office floors totalling 360,000 sq ft of net lettable area, comprising nine low-zone floors (on levels eight to 16) and 12 high-zone floors (on levels 22 to 33).

Aon will relocate from SGX Centre 1, where it occupies around 40,000 sq ft on four floors. Its lease in the building expires in late-2028.

Another tenant that has signed up at The Clifford is understood to be Squarepoint, a quantitative investment management, technology and trading group.

It is said to have leased three floors totalling 45,000 sq ft in the high zone, with flexibility to take an additional floor. This represents a major expansion for the group, which currently occupies about 23,000 sq ft on level 49 of CapitaSpring in Market Street. The lease, which is due for expiry around March or April next year, is being extended, say industry observers.

CICT owns the office component of CapitaSpring.

The Clifford will have 45,000 sq ft of retail space in basement one, level one and level two, part of level three and on the rooftop.

The project will be linked at basement one to Raffles Place MRT station.

At level two, the development will connect to the existing link across the road to OUE Tower.

data.title: Gold demand revives in India, China as price slide sparks bargain buying
data.description:
GOLD demand in top Asian hubs improved this week after prices fell to their lowest level in more than a year, drawing bargain-hunting jewellery and investment buyers to the market in India, while robust retail purchases in China kept local premiums firm.

International spot gold prices fell to their lowest level since August 2025 on Wednesday (Nov 25) after hot US inflation data cemented expectations of interest rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve.

In India, domestic gold prices were trading around 124,800 rupees per 10 g on Friday, after falling to 117,906 rupees earlier this week, the lowest level since October 28, 2025.

“Buyers were not expecting such a sharp price correction. The decline is now driving a pickup in jewellery purchases among retail consumers, while also boosting demand for coins and bars from investors,” said Chirag ​Thakkar, chief executive of bullion dealer Amrapali Group Gujarat.

Dealers quoted premiums of up to US$19 an ounce over official domestic prices this week, inclusive of 15 per cent import and 3 per cent sales levies, compared to the last week’s premium of up to US$17.

Jewellers are replenishing stocks as the price correction has raised expectations of stronger demand during the wedding season, said a Mumbai-based bullion dealer with a private bank.

In China, bullion traded at US$9-an-ounce premium over global benchmark prices.

“Dealers reported robust sales, with some shops running low on inventory, helping keep local premiums firm,” said Peter Fung, head of dealing at Wing Fung Precious Metals.

Meanwhile, China’s net gold imports via Hong Kong in October rose 1.6 per cent from the previous month, hitting their highest level since April, Hong Kong Census and Statistics Department data showed on Thursday.

In Singapore, gold traded between a US$0.50 discount and a US$1.80 premium this week, while in Hong Kong, gold was sold at a US$2 premium.

Elsewhere, in Japan, gold traded in a range from a US$0.50 discount to a US$0.50 premium this week. REUTERS

data.title: Singapore has not confirmed reports of Nvidia shipment halts: DPM Gan
data.description:
[SINGAPORE] Singapore has not confirmed reports that US chip giant Nvidia has halted shipments to the Republic, said Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong on Nov 27.

The government is in the process of engaging local companies to assess the impact of the United States’ latest chip curbs, and is working with America to explore how Singaporean firms can continue having secured access to high-end chips.

Businesses are also organising themselves and working with partners for continued chip access, Gan added.

He was speaking at a dialogue session at SPH Media’s Asia Future Summit, where he was asked about media reports that Nvidia had told its partners to stop shipping servers containing its chips to South-east Asian countries.

This followed the US’ announcement in November of a rule mandating that firms in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil obtain export licences for advanced chips, as America clamps down on what it sees as avenues for China to access these processors.

“We have repeatedly stated that Singapore does not want to become a conduit for illegal trade in any form,” Gan said, adding that the Republic was reviewing how it could strengthen regulations and monitoring to ensure this would not happen.

The government was still studying what such measures would look like, he said, as Singapore already had quite a comprehensive system to monitor companies’ activities here.

“But there are activities that are conducted outside of Singapore (which) we do not have information about”, which involves cooperation between countries, he added. Singapore hoped to strengthen cooperation and partnerships to share credible information, as it has always done, he said.

The Straits Times’ foreign editor Li Xueying, who moderated the session, asked about the reputational damage to Singapore, given how a “certain impression” appeared to have emerged despite the Republic having clearly outlined its measures to investigate violations and seek America’s cooperation.

Trust was important to Singapore as an international business hub, Gan said. “The fact that we launched an investigation, and the fact that we take legal action against those who flout our laws… I think that reflects our determination to safeguard our reputation.”

“But in order for us to enforce and to take real action, we need evidence,” he reiterated. “We do need cooperation from other countries to provide the information, provide evidence, because we can’t do investigations in other countries.”

Gan was speaking to an audience of about 370, including policymakers, business leaders and industry experts, at the annual conference jointly presented by The Straits Times, The Business Times, Lianhe Zaobao, Berita Harian and Tamil Murasu.

OCBC was the presenting sponsor for Asia Future Summit 2026, with Marina Bay Sands as the official venue partner and Amazon Web Services as the official cloud partner.

At the dialogue, Gan also addressed Singapore’s strategy towards the US’ changing tariff regime, from Liberation Day levies to various Section 301 and 232 duties.

“Our approach has not changed, and even now we have not changed,” he said, two days after the US proposed fresh levies of up to 20 per cent on Singapore over what it deemed structural excess capacity.

“Even as we negotiate, we have to be clear where our principles lie, and it will always be based on Singapore’s core interests.”

Gan said that Singapore thus far did not have an agreement on reciprocal trade with the US, referring to bilateral deals which Washington has negotiated with countries in exchange for a lower tariff rate.

The US does not necessarily require such an agreement to reduce tariffs – Washington said in its latest announcement that it is prepared to accept “other negotiations” to address its findings on excess capacity.

Gan said that negotiations were not guaranteed to succeed and would entail trade-offs that had to be weighed. “But it is also important for us to remember that every time when we negotiate, we must be prepared to walk away when the price they ask for is too high.”

Asked about the trend of economic warfare and weaponisation of technology amid US-China contestation – from 5G years earlier to AI chips more recently – Gan said “this new landscape that we are facing today is here to stay”.

The world has changed and is still changing, and it is important to strengthen resilience against volatility in a world where uncertainty has become a new norm, he added.

Singapore’s small size is an advantage as it helps the country move quickly, with its responsiveness to investors a key driving force for the Republic’s economic growth, he said.

Gan also noted that Asean – which in 2027 celebrates its 60th anniversary – could count its diversity as a source of strength.

“You can imagine if all 11 countries in Asean are producing exactly the same thing, we will be competing with each other and there will be no room for cooperation,” he said.

“But because of the diversity that we have in all 11 countries, we are complementary to one another, and if we are able to focus on complementarity and open up avenues of cooperation, that’s what will move Asean forward.” THE STRAITS TIMES

  • For more information, visit www.asiafuturesummit.com

data.title: AirAsia delays staff salary payments to end of month, internal email shows
data.description:
[HONG KONG/KUALA LUMPUR] AirAsia has told employees it will delay salary payments to the end of each month from November through March, according to an internal email seen by Reuters, as the airline takes measures to conserve cash and its Philippine unit cuts jobs.

The email, sent to Malaysia-based staff late last week by chief people officer Muhammad Khurram Zia, cited the need for a “temporary operational adjustment” at South-east Asia’s largest budget airline, which like its peers faces higher jet fuel costs.

Salary payments during the five-month period would be made on the 30th of each month or the last day of February, the email said.

It cited a “challenging environment” and asked employees for “patience and flexibility”.

The email’s contents were confirmed by two people familiar with the matter. One of the people said AirAsia had previously paid salaries earlier in the second half of each month.

AirAsia did not respond to a request for comment.

The Iran war has sent jet fuel prices soaring, putting airlines worldwide under their worst financial strain since the Covid-19 pandemic.

US low-cost carrier Spirit Airlines collapsed in May, Latvia’s airBaltic sought bankruptcy protection in September and Norway’s Norse Atlantic suspended flights on Thursday (Nov 26) as it looks for urgent short-term financing.

AirAsia Philippines announces layoffs

Shares in AirAsia, which employs about 26,000 people predominantly in Asia, have declined more than 70 per cent in 2026 as elevated fuel prices and foreign exchange losses squeezed its operations.

AirAsia Philippines said on Thursday it would reduce its workforce following sustained pressure on its operating costs, without specifying how many staff would be affected.

The airline said on Friday it remained fully operational and committed to serving the Philippine market. The planned workforce adjustment will not affect passenger flights, booking or other services, AirAsia Philippines general manager and president Anna Victoria Lu said in a statement.

The AirAsia Philippines Pilots’ Union filed notice of a strike after 90 pilots were retrenched, its president said in a video posted on social media on Thursday.

Philippine Labor Secretary Francis Tolentino confirmed receiving notice in a text message to Reuters.

AirAsia reported its third consecutive quarterly loss on Monday, though it was narrower than the prior quarter. Its cash and bank balances stood at 905 million ringgit (US$219.93 million) as at Sep 30, down 5 per cent from Jun 30.

In an investor presentation accompanying its results, the airline said it was taking measures to conserve cash, including suspending unviable routes and returning 25 planes to lessors.

It said more planes could exit its fleet in 2027, and a creditor restructuring was underway as part of a plan to reset the business before rebuilding in 2028.

AirAsia CEO Bo Lingam said on Monday that the third-quarter results suggested “the worst is behind us”, while cautioning that fourth-quarter fuel costs were expected to rise further.

Malaysia’s government has been weighing options to support AirAsia without putting public funds at risk, Reuters has previously reported.

The country’s finance ministry said on Thursday that it would ask AirAsia for priority over other lenders and strengthen oversight of the airline’s board and management if it decided to extend support. REUTERS

data.title: JPMorgan, BlackRock among those making bid to manage CPF savings
data.description:
JPMORGAN Asset Management, BlackRock and Endowus Singapore are the frontrunners to manage a slice of Singapore’s S$701 billion (US$543 billion) public pension fund.

The three firms submitted proposals to run a new investment programme that offers an alternative for members of the Central Provident Fund who want to earn more than the government-guaranteed return, according to people familiar with the matter.

The winners will be announced in the first half of 2027. Discussions are preliminary and no final decisions have been made, said the people, who asked not to be identified discussing private matters.

JPMorgan would partner with Singapore’s largest bank, DBS, in an extension of a retirement portfolio programme that was piloted in 2024. Endowus, an investment platform, is in talks to work with Capital Group on the CPF programme, said the people.

A spokesperson for the CPF Board said the evaluation process is ongoing, and it can’t comment on individual applications.

JPMorgan and Capital Group declined to comment. Endowus said it has been a digital adviser for investing CPF savings since 2019. BlackRock and DBS didn’t respond to requests for comment.

The investment plan was unveiled by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in this year’s budget speech as a way to deal with the country’s aging population, and will be launched in 2028.

The new programme will allow members to opt in to portfolio strategies that automatically adjust according to their age. As investors get older, the equity allocation will shift to lower-risk assets such as bonds, before being liquidated in phases by a set target date.

Currently, members have the option of manually picking investments, including bonds, stocks and unit trusts, from a list of more than 30 asset managers. As of September, just S$22 billion – or 3 per cent – of net assets were invested in this optional plan, according to the CPF website.

The bulk of CPF savings are invested by the pension board in Special Singapore Government Securities. Proceeds from these securities are pooled with other government funds, including from budget surpluses and land sales, and managed by sovereign wealth fund GIC for long-term returns. Members under 55 earn risk-free interest of up to 5 per cent a year.

Founded in 1955, the CPF is Singapore’s mandatory pension fund for citizens and permanent residents to support retirement, housing and health-care needs. There are more than two million active members, and over S$14 billion in CPF contributions were received in the third quarter. BLOOMBERG

data.title: Philippine trade deficit hits record as imports soar 50% in October
data.description:
THE PHILIPPINES posted a record trade deficit in October as a 50 per cent surge in imports outpaced another sharp rise in exports.

October’s trade deficit was US$6.95 billion, preliminary data from the Philippine Statistics Authority showed on Friday (Nov 27). That is the widest since 1980 and 65.6 per cent more than a year earlier, based on Bloomberg data.

Imports rose to a record-high US$17.52 billion, as electronics products soared 147.4 per cent and telecoms equipment surged 65.7 per cent.

Imports of mineral fuels and cereals also showed significant increases for the South-east Asian nation that relies heavily on imported oil and rice.

The imports jump outpaced another record-breaking month for exports, which rose 41.8 per cent to US$10.6 billion.

The artificial intelligence boom boosted demand for semiconductors and devices such as personal computers and smartphones.

The Philippine central bank forecasts a current account deficit of US$19.1 billion for 2026, before widening further to US$19.4 billion in 2027.

The peso was at 63.71 against the US dollar, flat from its close on Thursday. BLOOMBERG

data.title: Japan, Hong Kong banks set to improve in 2027 while Australia deteriorates: Fitch
data.description:
[SINGAPORE] Banking conditions across the Asia-Pacific (Apac) are set to remain broadly sound in 2027, though a divergence is emerging among the region’s developed markets, according to Fitch Ratings.

In its banking outlook reports for developed and emerging markets released on Thursday (Nov 26), the credit rating agency assigned “improving” outlooks to the banking sectors in Japan and Hong Kong, while downgrading Australia’s to “deteriorating”.

Meanwhile, the banking sector outlook across the region’s emerging markets was kept “neutral”, with the Philippines the sole market to receive an “improving” call.

“Fitch Ratings expects broadly stable operating conditions for most Apac developed-market banking systems in 2027, with higher interest rates supporting net interest margins (NIMs) and earnings in most markets,” the agency said in its developed markets report.

In Japan, continued interest-rate normalisation is a key tailwind for the country’s major banks. Fitch forecasts the country’s policy rate to reach 2 per cent by end-2027.

“Higher domestic interest rates and continued asset repricing are likely to strengthen earnings generation and internal capital formation, while a more active business environment provides additional revenue opportunities,” Fitch noted.

“Sustained inflation, wage growth and solid corporate activity should continue to support lending demand, transaction activity and fee-generating businesses,” the report added.

Meanwhile, Hong Kong’s banking sector, which entered 2026 on a “deteriorating” outlook before being revised to “neutral” in the first half of the year, was also upgraded to “improving” for 2027.

“Easing commercial real-estate market pressures – alongside solid wealth-management income and cross-border activity – underpin Hong Kong’s improvement,” Fitch said.

The agency expects Hong Kong banks’ core profitability to improve in 2027, as pressure on margins and asset quality recedes, while wealth-related fee-income growth remains solid.

“We expect credit costs to decline further over 2027, reflecting early signs of property-market stabilisation and the provisioning that banks have already built in prior years.”

Australia diverges

In contrast, Australia stands out as the sole developed market moving to a “deteriorating” outlook, from “neutral”.

“We expect a combination of higher-for-longer interest rates and a weakening labour market to weigh on asset quality, while strong competition and high investment requirements are likely to constrain earnings growth,” Fitch said.

Loan growth is also likely to slow, constrained by higher interest rates and decelerating economic growth.

Still, the agency offered reassurance on the sector’s buffers. “Losses should remain manageable, given a decade of conservative underwriting, a heavy weighting towards residential mortgages and strong collateral positions,” it said.

Singapore holds steady

Closer to home, Singapore banks remain on a “neutral” outlook.

“We expect Singapore banks to deliver another year of strong performance in 2027, building on robust results in 2026, while global uncertainty remains a downside risk,” Fitch said.

A higher Singapore Overnight Rate Average is likely to support NIMs, while sustained wealth-management inflows should drive mid to high single-digit growth in fee and commission income.

“Strong provision coverage and conservative underwriting standards leave banks well-positioned to absorb stresses should any emerge,” the agency added.

Emerging markets cushioned

Across emerging Asia-Pacific markets, eight of nine banking systems are on “neutral” outlooks.

Fitch said it expects financial performance for most Apac emerging market banking systems in 2027 to be broadly in line with 2026.

The Philippines is the lone emerging market with an “improving” banking sector, rebounding from weak economic growth and elevated consumer impairments in 2026.

“Accelerated public investments in infrastructure projects should drive economic growth and corporate loan demand in 2027,” Fitch said. It projected the Philippines’ loan growth to pick up to 11 per cent from 10 per cent, while credit costs decline to 1 per cent from 1.3 per cent.

China and Thailand both carry “neutral” outlooks for 2027 after entering 2026 on “deteriorating”.

For China’s banking sector, where system loan growth is projected at 5 to 6 per cent, Fitch said: “We expect NIMs to improve marginally, as a flat policy rate and lower deposit costs from repricing should more than offset pressure on loan yields.”

Thai banks are likewise set for steady performance as they gradually work through legacy bad debt.

Meanwhile, India and Indonesia remain among the region’s strongest growth markets, with double-digit loan expansion forecast at around 15 per cent for India in FY2028 and 10 per cent for Indonesia in 2027, although higher credit costs will limit profitability upside.

Looking ahead, Fitch flagged persistent inflation, tighter-for-longer monetary conditions, renewed geopolitical tensions and weaker global growth as key downside risks for Apac’s banking sector.

“Softer artificial intelligence-related demand or geopolitical shocks would pressure growth and asset quality, with South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong and Singapore most exposed,” the agency warned.

Nevertheless, resilient asset quality, generally adequate capital buffers and broadly stable profitability leave Apac banks well-positioned to weather these headwinds, Fitch said.
